Koniecpol Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Koniecpol, Poland

Demolished. Koniecpol, granted town rights in 1443, saw Jewish settlement begin in the early 17th century, growing to 45% (1,077) of the population by 1921. A late-1941 ghetto gathered about 1,600 Jews from Koniecpol and surrounding villages; following its liquidation on October 6, 1942, residents were deported to Treblinka. This cemetery, probably founded in the 19th century, was completely destroyed during WWII; postwar residential and industrial construction, including today's Municipal Services Department building, has left no surviving trace or tombstones.
